title: Operator channel in runner prompts: routing table + doctrine wiring
description:
Serves project fact A19. Edit ONLY skills/ticks/ (source of truth; never installed copies). Prose changes to the runner protocol so orchestrators use the operator channel (tk tell / tk ask / tk answer, shipped in epics 54v+d0d) in the right situations. Verify every command and flag you write against cmd/tk/cmd/*.go (learnings rule) — key contracts: tk tell exit 4 unconfigured (safe to call unconditionally); tk ask [--gate approve] [--timeout, exit 7 leaves tick awaiting+answerable] [--async / --collect --wait] [--escalate-after]; tk answer requires --from human on gates (runner-shaped actors refused).

1. references/agent-runner.md — new section "The operator channel" placed before "Human-in-the-loop ticks", with the routing table: requires/awaiting gate reached → tk ask --gate approve; blocked worker + frontier still moving → park (as today) + tk tell; blocked and frontier empty/stalling → tk ask (escalation); project checkpoint → tk tell report + tk ask sign-off; epic/run completion report → tk tell; planning/kickoff/retro conversations → never (human is in-session; use in-session tools). State the mechanical trigger: use the channel only when a pairing exists (tk channel status) AND the runner is executing, not planning; tk commands degrade safely when unconfigured so prompts may call them unconditionally. Add the bar-unchanged sentence: tk ask changes the latency of an answer, not the bar for needing one — a question planning could have resolved is still a planning miss and still lands in the retro interrupt audit. Wire the four existing spots by reference, minimally: "When an agent is blocked" (step for the two blocked rows), the action:await rows in Resuming a run, "Closing the epic" completion report (tk tell), and "Human-in-the-loop ticks"/gate-clearing (a channel answer or tk answer --from human IS a human decision relayed mechanically — same audit standard; workers never touch the channel, orchestrator only).
2. SKILL.md — one clause on the planning-is-interactive doctrine pointing at the new section; mention tk answer beside tk approve in "Assisting with Awaiting Ticks".
3. references/tick-patterns.md — in Human-in-the-loop ticks, one paragraph: a configured operator channel changes the ECONOMICS of the surviving gates (post-work approvals become one phone tap), not the triage; ask-early/block-late unchanged, --escalate-after noted.
4. Keep it channel-neutral: say "operator channel", never Telegram, except one pointer to docs/operator-channel.md for setup.

Acceptance is prose quality + accuracy: no invented flags, all wiring spots updated coherently, doctrine sentences present, diff confined to skills/ticks/.
